::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the MC-202 is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **MC-202** was made by **Roland** in **1983** (Wikipedia, "Roland MC-202").
- Wikipedia: "It was the first groovebox." It has a small synth inside and a sequencer.
- It has **2 channels**, holds about 2600 steps and can save to tape (MC-202 manual, p. 5).

## Its sound

- Each note has a **step time** (how long until the next note) and a **gate time** (how long the note sounds) (manual, p. 10).
- A quarter note is **24**; the default step is 24 and gate 12 (manual, pp. 15-16).
- A gate of 0 is a **rest** (manual, p. 19).
- **Accent** and **portamento** (glide) are stored with the notes (manual, pp. 5, 29).

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Gate time is…</b></p><ul><li>How long the note sounds</li><li>How long until the next note</li><li>The tempo</li><li>The volume</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 10.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>On the MC-202 a quarter note is…</b></p><ul><li>24</li><li>4</li><li>120</li><li>16</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 15.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>A gate of 0 is…</b></p><ul><li>A rest</li><li>The loudest note</li><li>A slide</li><li>An error</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 19.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Wikipedia calls the MC-202 the first…</b></p><ul><li>Groovebox</li><li>Synthesizer</li><li>Drum machine</li><li>Computer</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
```
